artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system, with Bruhat order $\le$ and Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials $\{P_{u,v}(q) : u\le v \text{ in } W\}$. For $u\le v$ in $W$, does there always exist a Coxeter system $(W',S')$ and an element $w'\in W'$ such that
$$P_{u,v}(q) \;=\; P_{e',w'}(q),$$
where $e'$ denotes the identity element of $W'$? In other words, is every Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial of an arbitrary Bruhat interval realized as the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial of a lower interval $[e',w']$ in some (possibly different) Coxeter system?
artifact.status_search_result: The question, attributed to Björner, asks whether every Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial of a Bruhat interval can be realized as one of a lower interval in some Coxeter system. It is a strong refinement of the combinatorial invariance conjecture. While combinatorial invariance has been established for lower intervals (Brenti–Caselli–Marietti, Delanoy) and recent work (e.g., the BBDVW conjecture for lower intervals, 2024–2026) addresses related cases, no proof or counterexample to Björner's "reduction to lower intervals" question appears in the literature; it is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: BBDVW Conjecture for Kazhdan–Lusztig Polynomials of Lower Intervals
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials of lower intervals; combinatorial invariance for lower intervals proved by Brenti–Caselli–Marietti and Delanoy.
status_evidence.claim: Lower-interval cases of related conjectures have been resolved, but the general reduction question remains open.

status_evidence.title: The BBDVW Conjecture for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials of lower intervals
status_evidence.snippet: Studies KL polynomials of lower intervals [e,w] without claiming reducibility of arbitrary intervals to lower intervals.
status_evidence.claim: Reduction of arbitrary KL polynomials to lower-interval KL polynomials is not established.
